title: Power Pages: enhanced authorisation maps web roles and site users to Dataverse security
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, preview behaviour, enablement path and licensing statements are supported by Microsoft's documentation. The governance checklist mentions column security and auditing controls that are not represented in the controls table, a minor completeness issue.

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified at 2026-10-16T19:08:35.
Power Pages continues to use contacts and web roles with enhanced authorisation.
claims.quote: When enhanced authorization is enabled, Power Pages continues to use site users (contacts) and web roles to define access.

claims.claim: Enhanced authorisation maps each contact to a corresponding Dataverse system user.
claims.quote: With enhanced authorization enabled, each contact is mapped to a corresponding system user in Dataverse.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Each web role is mapped to a corresponding Dataverse security role.
claims.quote: Each web role is associated with a corresponding Dataverse security role

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Dataverse evaluates permissions directly and returns only records the site user is permitted to access.
claims.quote: Dataverse evaluates permissions based on the site user's roles and returns only the records the user is allowed to access.

claims.claim: The standard model checked permissions in Power Pages after retrieving data using an elevated application user.
claims.quote: In the standard authorization model, Power Pages evaluates table and record permissions after data retrieval from Dataverse by using the Power Pages application user that runs with elevated privilege

claims.claim: Enhanced authorisation removes the extra Power Pages permission-checking layer.
claims.quote: This change removes the extra permission checking layer at Power Pages and ensures alignment with Dataverse's native security model.

claims.claim: Dataverse operations use impersonation to execute on behalf of the site user.
claims.quote: Dataverse operations execute on behalf of the site user by using impersonation rather than the application user.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Plug-ins run as the calling user unless explicitly configured otherwise.
claims.quote: If any plugin is registered, it runs as the calling user unless explicitly configured otherwise.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: When auditing is enabled on a Dataverse table, site operations are tracked under the respective site user.
claims.quote: When auditing is enabled on a Dataverse table, any operation performed from the Power Pages site tracks under the respective site user.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Power Pages Web API column-level permissions are bypassed under enhanced authorisation.
claims.quote: Column level permissions that you configure in the Power Pages for Web API are bypassed

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Dataverse column security profiles apply instead of Power Pages Web API column-level permissions.
claims.quote: Column level permissions that you configure in the Power Pages for Web API are bypassed, and Dataverse column security profiles are used instead.
